॥ Om, and from the specific attribute, Om. ॥ 1/2/12 ॥

“Whoever knows the imperishable Brahman, which is the bridge for the wise, that is the Supreme.” Thus it is stated. “It is not possible to describe its qualities separately due to its infinite nature. Therefore, the term ‘Brahman’ serves to encompass all. Hence, this term ‘Brahman’ is specifically an attribute of Vishnu. For, the qualities are infinite, and from whom the others are not distinct, that is the imperishable, all-pervading one.” Thus it is stated in the Brahma Upanishad.

Nor is the identity (samanyo) of the individual soul (jiva) with the Supreme Self (Atman) asserted. “The Self is true, the individual soul is true, the distinction is true, the distinction is true, the distinction is true. I shall not ascend, I shall not ascend, I shall not ascend.” Thus it is stated in the Paingira Shruiti. “For, the Self is the Supreme, independent, and possessing superior qualities, whereas the individual soul is of limited power, dependent, and inferior.” Thus it is stated in the Bhalleya Shruiti. “Just as the distinction between the Lord (Ishvara) and the individual soul (jiva) is true by definitive conclusion, so too, you are fit to speak my true words here.” “Just as the Lord and the individual soul are truly distinct from each other, may the gods, along with the companions of Kesava, protect me with that truth.” Thus, and so on, the distinction is not false. ॥ 12 ॥
